Battle after bitter battle: this body was little more than <ruby>wreckage<rt>scrap</rt></ruby> already.
Ordinary sensation had long since gone. Every nerve was filled with the same endless exhaustion, as though I must go on dragging a stone without end.

Pain.
Misery.
No more. Not one second more could be borne.

Sleep now. Surely, after all this fighting, a man could be allowed that much.

What was the objection, then?
My opponent's way of being—I accepted it. Respected it, even.

For what, then, must I go on fighting?

en.html:
I knew what my armor meant to say. No need to hear it to the end.
I had felt it already.

...Little by little, we were being pushed back.
The balance of strength was moving, steadily, towards our defeat.

<ruby>Muramasa's<rt>My</rt></ruby> strength had not diminished.
Flesh and bone were being pared away; a year of remaining life became a second of vitality. At that cost, her fighting power remained at its peak.

But <ruby>Masamune<rt>the enemy</rt></ruby> was not content merely to remain at a peak.
One strongest blow, then a stronger one. And after that, one stronger still.

Each exchange made it stronger. <ruby>More powerful<rt>Stronger</rt></ruby>. <ruby>More unyielding<rt>Stronger</rt></ruby>.

Perhaps this was what <ruby>Ichijou Ayane<rt>my enemy</rt></ruby> had finally revealed: the true nature of a hero.

A hero did not suffer defeat. <ruby>In the end, a hero always won<rt>・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>.
Hardship upon hardship, one step after another up the stairs—and in the end, the power to bring the enemy down would surely be obtained.

Continue like this, and I would lose.

As a human being, I accepted it. With profound admiration, even.

Continue like this, and I would lose.

But a combatant could not stop at admiration. For that mind, accepting the situation was where the work of breaking it began.

How to overturn it, then?
————From the beginning, there had been one move.

Let the enemy climb the stairs. Mine was to reach a height no amount of climbing could approach.
No need to remain there, balanced on a needle's point. All my strength, for one instant only. The instant of one blow, that was enough.

I had only to stand there <ruby>with<rt>by means of</rt></ruby> a <ruby>killing technique<rt>full stop</rt></ruby>.

With an electromagnetic draw into which I put my whole being.

The worst course.
The most foolish.

At the very end, that was what I chose.

No art I attempted would help.
No trap I laid would have any power.

Ichijou's justice would not yield to such things.

It was a blazing sun. Petty interference could promise only self-destruction: burned away before one even touched it.

If there was a means of extinguishing the sun, it was one alone.
Strike it with a mass equal to its own, or greater.

If Ichijou possessed unyielding justice,
and Masamune an unbreakable Divine Art,

then there was nothing for it but to shatter both together.

That was the only move!

The descending flash had come within an inch of its head. It stopped it with its sword, raised as a shield.

...That sight exceeded the laws of this world.
How did it stop a stroke that was light itself? How did it continue to sustain it?

Was justice a thing of such power?


But. Even so—

I would cut justiceyou down!

en.html:
Your soul is not yet exhausted.
Neither is mine.

With arteries and several organs burst, this body is already counting down. Yet it still holds my soul to the living world.

I will stake all that remains to answer your will.
I will carry my own will through.

We asked.

Justice.
Evil.
We asked their meaning, their significance, their truth.

—Let us go on asking.

To the end.
Until Kageaki Minato and Ichijou Ayane are spent.

That question—upon which surely so many before us staked their lives: kings, monks, knights, widows, scholars, poets, merchants, farmers, beggars—

Let us pursue its answer.
Straight ahead, down the road each of us has chosen.

ja.html:
お前の魂が尽きないように、
　俺の魂もまだ残っている。

　動脈と臓器のいくつかが弾けた肉体は既に秒読み。
　しかしまだ魂を現世に繋ぎ止めている。

　この、残る全てを賭してお前の意思に報いよう。
　俺自身の意思を貫徹しよう。

　俺達は問うた。

　正義。
　邪悪。
　その意味を、意義を、真実を問うた。

　――問い続けよう。

　最後まで。
　湊斗景明と綾弥一条が尽き果てるまで。

　その命題、
　過去にもきっと数多の人間が――王侯が、僧侶が、
騎士が、寡婦が、学者が、詩人が、商人が、農夫が、
乞食が――身命を賭したのであろう問いの、

　答えを追い求めよう。
　ただ真っ直ぐに、選んだこの道を駆け抜けて。
